claim.why_it_matters: The 20-21 row of the WHEN-COMPILED returned-value table is no longer a table row, so any tool or reader consuming the 15.99.3 table sees only positions 1 through 19 and the last two character positions of the 21-character returned value fall out of the structure. The transcription already has the correct convention for this exact situation — the identical CURRENT-DATE table split across pages 864/865 restarts with a '| **Character Positions** | **Contents** |' header row and continues the table — so page 968 is an inconsistent degradation, not a house style.

verdict.reasoning:
REFUTED. The difference is table-continuation markup across a page break, not a content discrepancy.

(1) TEXT PRESENCE — nothing is lost, moved, or altered. I rendered PDF page 968 (printed folio 938) at 300 dpi and read it. The page carries exactly three blocks: the '20-21 ...' entry, rule 2), and rule 3). The markdown page-968 block (specs/ISO_COBOL.md lines 38693-38702) carries the same three blocks in the same order, and line 38698 reproduces the 20-21 sentence word for word — the '20-21' position label, 'in the range 00 through 59', the '+' / '–' disjunction, and the closing "If character position 17 is '0', the value 00 is returned." Rules 2) and 3) likewise match verbatim. The entry is still under 15.99.3 rule 1), still immediately after the rows it continues, still before rule 2). Nothing is misplaced, so the filed kind is wrong on its face.

(2) GLYPH CHECK, as instructed. Reading the printed glyphs on the page render: the quoted characters are '+', an en-dash-width minus, and '0'. I then dumped the non-ASCII code points of markdown line 38698 and got exactly one, U+2013 EN DASH, at the sign position — the same code point used in the sibling rows on page 967 (line 38688) and in the CURRENT-DATE table (line 34764). The sign/choice glyph is transcribed correctly and consistently. No indicator is lost. (Recording this because a superseded verdict previously in this file asserted the markdown carried U+FFFD mojibake here; that assertion is false — the byte dump shows U+2013, and the replacement character seen in terminal output is a console rendering artifact.)

(3) THE CLAIM'S CENTRAL SUPPORTING ARGUMENT DOES NOT SURVIVE INSPECTION. The claim rests on page 968 being an inconsistent degradation versus 'the identical CURRENT-DATE table split across pages 864/865', where the markdown restarts with a '| **Character Positions** | **Contents** |' header. I rendered PDF page 865 (folio 835) to test this. That page REPRINTS the bold 'Character Positions' / 'Contents' column headings above its 20-21 row. PDF page 968 does NOT reprint them — it opens with the bare '20-21' entry directly under the running head. The two markdown pages therefore differ because the two source pages are printed differently: at 865 the transcription is faithfully copying a header that is actually on the page, not applying a continuation convention it then abandoned at 968. The 'identical situation' premise is materially inaccurate, and with it the 'inconsistent degradation, not a house style' conclusion.

(4) WHAT REMAINS is that the PDF's 20-21 entry sits in the same two-column geometry as the rows on page 967 (narrow left position column, contents hang-indented to a common left edge), so it is visually a continued table row, while the markdown emits it as a paragraph. That is exactly the page-break/formatting class the verification rules direct me to reject: the position-to-contents mapping survives intact in the markdown via the leading '20-21' label, and no reader derives a different rule for the WHEN-COMPILED returned value from either source. Meaning is unchanged.
verdict.corrected_description: Not a PDF-vs-markdown content discrepancy — reject from the ledger as filed. The full 20-21 entry of the 15.99.3 WHEN-COMPILED returned-value table is transcribed verbatim, in the correct section and order, with its '20-21' label and its '+' / U+2013 / '0' glyphs intact; it is merely emitted as a paragraph rather than continued as a pipe-table row after the 967/968 page break. Nothing is missing or misplaced, and meaning is unchanged. If the reconciliation later wants machine-extractable tables end to end, reopening the table on page 968 would be a cosmetic markup improvement (kind: table-continuation-markup, severity: cosmetic), but it does not belong at structural severity. Two corrections to the original write-up: (a) the claimed precedent is not the identical situation — PDF page 865 reprints the 'Character Positions / Contents' column headings above its 20-21 row while PDF page 968 does not, so the markdown header row at page-865 is transcribed from the source rather than a continuation convention abandoned at 968; and (b) any suggestion that the sign glyph is degraded here is wrong — markdown line 38698 carries a proper U+2013 en dash, matching the sibling rows.
